1.title: “Very fine people” = Trump called neo-Nazis fine people
1.who: Widespread media framing; Joe Biden campaign ads/speeches; Sen. Chuck Schumer and many other politicians
1.claim: That Trump called neo-Nazis / white supremacists at Charlottesville “very fine people” (or “very good people”)
1.why: In the Aug. 15, 2017 remarks, Trump said there were “very fine people on both sides,” then explicitly: “I’m not talking about the neo-Nazis and the white nationalists, because they should be condemned totally.” Snopes rated the claim that he called neo-Nazis “very fine people” **False**. Separately, his “both sides” framing remains widely criticized.
1.full:
“Very fine people” = Trump called neo-Nazis fine people
- **Who:** Widespread media framing; Joe Biden campaign ads/speeches; Sen. Chuck Schumer and many other politicians
- **Claim:** That Trump called neo-Nazis / white supremacists at Charlottesville “very fine people” (or “very good people”)
- **Why false/misleading:** In the Aug. 15, 2017 remarks, Trump said there were “very fine people on both sides,” then explicitly: “I’m not talking about the neo-Nazis and the white nationalists, because they should be condemned totally.” Snopes rated the claim that he called neo-Nazis “very fine people” **False**.
